doc_summary: A short blog post defining out-of-context reasoning (OOCR) in LLMs as reaching conclusions requiring non-trivial reasoning that is not present in the context window, and pointing to a full primer elsewhere. It contains little on evaluation design or realism.

items.claim: Evans frames generalization and alignment questions around whether models reach conclusions via reasoning that is not visible in the context window, so tests should probe forward-pass or training-time reasoning rather than only chain-of-thought.
items.quote: It’s when an LLM reaches a conclusion that requires non-trivial reasoning but the reasoning is not present in the context window. The reasoning could instead take place in the forward pass or during the training process.

items.claim: Prefers evidence about reasoning that does not appear in context over in-context reasoning traces because intermediate steps in context would not show what the model can do internally.
items.quote: The name (“out-of-context reasoning”) is chosen to contrast with in-context reasoning (also called “in-context learning”), where intermediate reasoning steps do appear in context.

items.claim: Evans treats OOCR as a concept tied to both LLM generalization and AI alignment, so claims are framed around safety implications and not capability alone.
items.quote: Out-of-context reasoning (OOCR) is a concept relevant to LLM generalization and AI alignment.
